A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BA-LoRA. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original NLG and NLU evaluations, regularizer ablations, rank comparisons, and feature visualizations in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds NLU ablations, regularized baseline comparisons, and regularization-weight sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same PiSSA initialization, three regularizers, and NLU/NLG objectives. The added partial-SVD sentence documents an implementation optimization without specifying a revised BA-LoRA objective or adaptation rule; the regularized LoRA/DoRA variants are evaluated as comparisons.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluated task coverage remain unchanged: mathematical reasoning, code generation, conversation, GLUE, and GLUE-X. The new analyses reuse existing coverage. Appendix A.3 discusses noise categories from literature without introducing evaluated noise scenarios.

E2.justification: The DeBERTa comparison in Table 2 expands from three to nine baselines, adding BitFit, HAdapter, PAdapter, LoHA, DoRA, and AdaLoRA. New Table 10 also evaluates DoRA and regularized LoRA/DoRA against BA-LoRA on LLaMA-2-7B, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: The reported main NLU comparison drops the RoBERTa-large configuration and retains DeBERTa-v3-base. Added protocols include NLU single-regularizer controls and individual regularization-weight sweeps from 10^-6 to 10^-2 on LLaMA-2-7B. Existing experiments retain their stated metrics, training budgets, and settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds NLU component ablations on DeBERTa-v3-base (Table 5), tests whether regularizers benefit LoRA and DoRA beyond PiSSA (Table 10), and examines coefficient sensitivity (Figure 5). These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence beyond v2's retained NLG ablations, rank analysis, and feature visualizations.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages from three independent experiments and specify three random seeds for the GLUE experiments in Appendix B.4. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared Tables 1, 3, and 4 and retained DeBERTa rows in Table 2 are numerically unchanged, while the RoBERTa results disappear. Substantial new results include baseline scores, NLU single-regularizer averages of 89.78, 89.65, and 89.59 (Table 5), GSM8K scores of 49.26 for LoRA+Reg and 52.80 for DoRA+Reg (Table 10), and coefficient-sensitivity curves.

T1.justification: The SVD formulation, regularizer definitions, and objectives in Equations 1–13 are unchanged. Neither the main-text additions nor the appendix additions introduce new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: PiSSA-based BA-LoRA uses three regularizers to mitigate catastrophic inheritance and improve NLG/NLU performance. Additional comparisons and analyses support these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new comparisons as evidence that regularizers help beyond PiSSA and explains deterioration at large coefficients through excessive constraints on learning (Appendix C.3–C.4). It also discusses NLU component contributions. The limitations and future-work discussion remain unchanged despite relocation.

D1.justification: V3 newly states that partial SVD computes the top-k singular values for the NLG regularizer. It removes v2's paragraph identifying adapter placement in RoBERTa and DeBERTa. Hardware, most hyperparameter disclosures, and code/model access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 expands the supporting literature on duplication, corruption, contamination, imbalance, and harmful content, adding works such as Carlini et al. (2022), Hernandez et al. (2022), and Sun et al. (2024). The main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 removes the standalone baselines subsection, rewrites the NLU comparison passage, and adds background and analysis subsections with corresponding contents updates. Most existing exposition, including the method and conclusion, remains verbatim.

P2.justification: Table 2 is reorganized around methods; tables gain revised rules and second-best underlining. V3 adds Tables 5, 9, and 10 and Figure 5. Existing plots are retained and repositioned or renumbered, with the overall document layout preserved.

improvement.justification: The broader baseline comparison and new component, transfer, and sensitivity analyses better support the benefits of regularization (Tables 2, 5, and 10; Figure 5). The gain is limited by removing the RoBERTa-large results while retaining their appendix setup, and by leaving the central evidence for mitigating pre-training noise indirect. Overall, empirical support improves without resolving the main interpretive limitation.
